campaign: Integrated validation, phase 2: bounded capability gains and evidence-gated simplification
doctrine:
overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data, promote or revert), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The milestone is the loop itself (improvement-loop): from there, the scorecard's gaps generate the work.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing owner and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing owner can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced.

A change's landing cost is read from its diff, not declared, as three independent effects, each checked against the diff: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost (20 minutes to over an hour a landing), so false lane reach is cut. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a user-facing result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Before a batch lands, the packages its device lanes will run run on the device first, so a failure shows early. Guards are re-acquired once after the last surface batch of a run of them. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the owner reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

Landing speed is protected by observing it, not by a rule. Each structural boundary (a changed path's lanes, a package kept off the inference surface) is pinned as an invariant row in one table per kind, never as a new test function or a snapshot of today's lists. At each periodic review the gate's measured lines in git log are read: the share of landings that reached no lane, and executed versus cached package counts. A rise means a misplaced check or a new false reach, fixed by moving it and adding a table row. There are no time budgets or timeouts, no ratchet baselines, and no separate tracking subsystem.

items.title: Train on unpaired preference feedback with KTO

steps.title: Train on unpaired preference feedback with KTO
steps.rationale:
Split from preference-loss-variants on 2026-09-30. ORPO and SimPO landed there as modes of the DPO objective. KTO does not fit the paired preference data shape.

KTO (Ethayarajh et al. 2024) is L = E[λ_y − v(x,y)], with r = log πθ(y|x) − log πref(y|x).
- The KL estimate z0 = max(0, mean of r over mismatched pairs (x_i, y_j), j≠i) is taken within a microbatch, with no gradient through it.
- For a desirable completion v = λ_D·σ(β(r − z0)); for an undesirable one v = λ_U·σ(β(z0 − r)).

What the current path lacks:
1. Unpaired data: records of prompt, completion and a desirable or undesirable label. This needs a new dataset kind and processor, plus its materialize path in trainingworkflow/data.go. The preference-token-pair processor, parsePreferences and trainingdata.PreferencePair all require a chosen and a rejected completion.
2. More than one prompt per step. unitBatchPolicy steps once per pair. KTO needs microbatches of at least 2, sequences spliced from one example's prompt and another's completion (scored under both policy and reference), and gradients summed across examples. sequenceGradientSum could extend to this.
3. λ_D and λ_U in PreferencePolicy. The paper advises λ_D·n_D / (λ_U·n_U) between 1 and 4/3.
4. A held-out judge for unpaired records, since the current slice scores pairs by DPO loss.

Do not substitute TRL's kto_pair: its matched-pair KL term carries gradient, so it is not the paper's definition.

Serves: preference training on unpaired feedback (thumbs-up and thumbs-down data). Disappears: nothing. Evidence: the held-out unpaired slice judges it. Batch: surface (densecausal, trainingprogram).

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): all (densecausal and trainingprogram are surface).

Owner review 2026-09-30: ordered by user value and held-out availability. After e4b-full-parameter-trainer: its held-out unpaired preference set is still to be chosen.

SQA 2026-09-30, SQA-064 (P2): score-only dense forwards keep training snapshots they never use; drop them where only a score is needed. Note: densecausal and trainingprogram left the inference surface on 2026-09-30, so this row no longer expires guards.

items.title: Have every GPU user take the device claim lanes wait on

budget.reason: the swap launcher's wait for device admission

steps.title: Have every GPU user take the device claim lanes wait on
steps.rationale:
Three sessions share one GPU. Preview servers started through launch.json hold the device while gate lanes time out behind them, and on 2026-09-23 a server of unknown origin was killed to free it. A served model should hold the same claim, so a lane waits for it and names it (01cbf544) instead of timing out. 2026-09-25: the device lane of 69368990 failed 'physical resource is already reserved' in devicemath while two other gate processes held the GPU, and passed unchanged on re-run; a claim every GPU user takes turns that into a wait with a named holder instead of a failed lane and a manual re-run. Found 2026-09-26: every CUDA context already takes the shared device claim (driver.ContextCreate calls processcontrol.ShareResource), so a served model holds it for its context's life, and a timed-out exclusive wait already names its holders (01cbf544, TestResourceWaitNamesItsHolders). What remains is proof, not mechanism: a device test that a served model's context holds the claim an exclusive reservation then waits on.

Serves: loop speed. Disappears: the unclaimed GPU users that cause lane refusals. Batch: host.

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): device, model-journey.

Consolidated 2026-09-30 (owner review) with recovery-failures-seen: its remaining proof, a served model's context holding the claim an exclusive reservation waits on, is the ownership case of that row's foreign-gate drill, and lands with it. Observed 2026-09-30: while longform -guard held the GPU, cmd/train's route tests (TestTrainRoutesReachTheMediaTrainers, TestSeq2SeqRoutePublishesCheckpoint, TestThoughtBankRoutePublishesCheckpoint), run with -short and without OVERGO_CUDA_TEST, failed at once with 'processcontrol: physical resource is already reserved: GPU-...' instead of waiting for the holder. So any landing whose test stage runs cmd/train during a guard or device run is refused by the machine, not by the change. The proof this row owes includes those host-stage tests waiting on the claim, not failing.

Built 2026-10-01 (scratchpad deviceclaim.patch, +31 nodes): driver.ContextCreate runs its claim through processcontrol.AwaitResource, so a context waits for an exclusive holder instead of failing 'physical resource is already reserved'. The wait takes no lock between attempts; it uses context.Background(), since device.New has about 95 call sites and no context, so it ends with the holder or the process but never names the holder. Naming it needs a context threaded through device.New, a follow-up. Proof: host, processcontrol's TestRecoveryDrills rows (waits on an exclusive holder; an exclusive waits on and names a context's claim); device, TestCUDAContextSharedAdmission in the receipt. It is a surface and pinned-media change (internal/cuda/driver/driver_windows.go, before 668b17c5..., after 3b387558...), so it rides the next surface batch with the transcription recipe and its own reviewed delta.

items.title: Narrow the inference surface one responsibility at a time

steps.title: Keep non-text capability edits out of the inference surface
steps.rationale:

Measured 2026-09-23: the split (a capabilityrecipe package modelrecipe does not import, with the text path compiling against a text-only catalog) renames symbols in 79 files, several on pinned media runtime paths, so it waits on reviewed-delta-registry. It still cannot keep a NEW task off the surface: recipe/schema.go (task constants, validateTask) and recipecontract/modality.go stay reachable from inference. Adding RAE's modules would be protected; adding a task would not. Re-measure 2026-09-27 after gate-small-cutover: the gate's own records drive most store growth and evidence churn, so this row may no longer be needed.

Re-scoped 2026-09-30 (owner review): narrow the surface incrementally, one concrete responsibility per change, each moved to its existing owner:
- composition's graft training;
- densecausal's training half;
- modelrecipe's dataset responsibility, to dataset;
- the capability tables.
Each change verifies three things separately: preserved behaviour (its tests), the build and test closure, and the surface invalidation (inferencesurface.Moves on its diff). Guards are re-acquired once after the last of a run of these. Measured 2026-09-30 (change 1 built, graft training moved to trainingworkflow; patch surface1.patch in the master-lead scratchpad): it takes only capabilityruntime and jsonabbrev out of the closure (69 to 67 packages). densecausal, trainingprogram and trainingdata stay because composition/chain.go, the Tier-0 chain probe, uses densecausal's forward half. So change 2 is the chain probe, not densecausal's training half: moving it to its owner drops 8 more packages (agenttool, densecausal, devicemath, hfbpe, operation, trainingdata, trainingprogram, workflowruntime). Moving candidate realization too drops bridgetrain, hostoptimizer and optimizer. Then modelrecipe's dataset responsibility and the capability tables. runrecord/generation.go:59's comment still names composition.RecordViability; fix it in the batch that reaches thoughtbank and integration anyway.

Measured 2026-09-30, not landed (patch surface5.patch in the master-lead scratchpad):
- In September, 8 of 153 surface moves came only through modelrecipe's capability tables. RAE 9f5ea65be, the linear entries dde56a6a2 and e7ee897a9, speech-assemble 674f096ee, VQA 1a2da932b, and the audio builders a2df8940b, d68490754 and 6d85fc6b6. Each cost a guard re-acquisition.
- A cut is blocked because candidate_recipe_derivation.go (production code in modelrecipe) calls CapabilityDefinition, and many binaries link modelrecipe without linking mediacapability. So moving a table out needs either registration at init in the owner package, or the 79-file split.
- The built cut registers only RAE's image-gen modules from internal/rae at init (+38 nodes). It covers 1 of 7 generation families, and it adds a second way to declare a capability beside the tables. That is not landed, per the owner's subtraction-first review.
- Options with costs:
  (1) Every image and video family through one registration seam: about 45 files, including pinned media paths that need reviewed deltas (latentimage and sensenovarecipe runtime_cuda_windows.go, latentvideo production.go, diffusionimage and oscillatorimage runtime.go, sensenovarecipe activate.go).
  (2) A task-keyed seam for linear capabilities: image embedding is about 40 lines; forecast and generation fixtures hit import cycles in 12 test packages.
  (3) Audio builders: renames in about 21 files, no pinned paths.
  (4) New tasks stay on the surface through recipe/schema.go and recipecontract/modality.go whatever is done.
- Recommendation: take this step only as (1) plus (3) in one registration mechanism that replaces the tables, not beside them, when the next non-text capability lands anyway. Until then, the 8 moves a month cost guard re-acquisitions that are batched once per run.

items.title: Move live-evidence acceptance tests off the landing path

steps.title: Move live-evidence acceptance tests off the landing path
steps.rationale:
Owner review 2026-09-27. Measured: 088a4774c's test stage re-ran 17 suites for 6 min 56 s (audioparity 376 s, cmd/compatibility 192 s, capabilityruntime 122 s, modelintake 119 s, server 71 s) because plan -stop had written a record into the live store at 17:56:23; the next plan-only landing, with no store write before it, ran 4 packages in 40 s. Suites that read the live store re-run on every store write, and their verdict depends on the machine's store rather than the commit. The gate runs go test with OVERGO_DATA_ROOT pointing at an empty scratch directory and OVERGO_AUDIO_REFERENCE_STORE unset (construction: no test can reach the live store through the environment); the 16 test files that name the store by path (overgodb-store, gitauthority.CanonicalOvergoDBDirectory) become hermetic on fixtures or scratch stores, or move off the landing path to the scheduled scorecard and validate, where live-store checks belong. Predicted effect: landings stop paying for store writes; a narrow landing's test stage stays near a minute. Measured 2026-09-27 before starting: with the data root pointed at an empty directory, 133 tests in 77 files across 12 packages fail (cmd/compatibility 32 files, internal/audioparity 19, internal/evaluation 10, speechsynth, server and others): retained-evidence acceptance tests and a few live model-file tests. They re-run when the evidence changes, which is correct; the measured 7-minute landing came from a control record (plan -stop) written into the evidence store, which stop-state-out-of-store removes. Moving them means splitting mixed files across 12 packages and a scheduled evidence run. Do it only if dev-loop measurement shows real evidence writes costing landings. Re-raised 2026-09-27 under landing-wall-budget: the four slowest suites a landing re-runs are these, and they re-run on dependency changes as well as store writes, so the stop-file fix alone does not bring landings under the budget. Updated 2026-09-27 after 32ad2b892: the store-write cause is gone. The data lives outside the module folder, so a store write re-runs nothing. The audio acceptances run in their own lane (780d83550). What remains is hermeticity: these suites' verdicts depend on the machine's data. That does not speed up landings, because a lane would run exactly when their code changes, as go test does now. So the row ranks after the user-visible fixes. Measured 2026-09-28 after the lanes landed: go test ./... with OVERGO_DATA_ROOT on an empty folder fails 92 tests in 12 packages: cmd/compatibility 56 (40 top-level accepted-evidence and acceptance projections, opening the store through retainedReferenceStore in 34 places and dataroot.Resolve in about 36), internal/evaluation 16, internal/speechsynth 7, internal/server 4, internal/audioparity 2, and one each in oscillatorimage, modelintake, dataset, capabilityruntime, cmd/smoke-lane, cmd/longform and cmd/benchmark-report. The work: consolidate each package's live-store entry into one helper behind testskip.StoreAcceptance, and run the packages in a store lane (without the five failing audits, tracked in refresh-accepted-evidence). The benefit is hermeticity only: with the data outside the module, a lane runs these exactly when go test does now. Ranked after plan-tool-plain-data.

Serves: loop speed. Disappears: live-evidence suites on the landing path. Batch: host.

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): the lanes of the suites it moves.

Owner review 2026-09-30: justified as robustness unless the gate's timing shows a saving.

SQA 2026-09-30: SQA-056 (P2): a registered GGUF that fails to read is reported as an inapplicable test; it must fail. SQA-044 and SQA-037 are handled in compatibility-into-validate and lane-cost.

steps.rationale: The overgo_vae lane (branch codex/overgo_vae, campaign overgo_rsi_with_vae, design docs/overgo_rsi_with_vae.md) runs the native-Go latent RSI and PEARL campaign with its own plan in its own worktree. decisions.question: Download the unquantized google/gemma-4-12B-it? The 12B FP8 twins score 0.5-1.2 nats per token worse than E4B on the guard corpus while overgo's 12B graph matches the transformers reference, so the third-party quant is the suspect.
options: Keep only the FP8 twins and record the gap

decisions.question: Fetch RAE's reference code (github.com/bytetriper/RAE) and its encoder checkpoints? models/RAE-collections holds the decoders, DiTs and latent statistics but neither of those.

Close fp8 prefill's 21% gap to bf16 (3,036 against 3,837 prompt tok/s on the 12B) how? An FP8-by-FP8 GEMM quantizes activations to e4m3, a numerics change that needs held-out evaluation; a kernel that expands e4m3 to f16 in registers keeps today's numbers but is custom tensor-core work.
The capability census changed from 209 recorded identities to 220 live ones. Record a disposition that accepts the live census as the new denominator?
options: Review the 11 new identities, then accept
Accept the live census as it stands
decisions.recommendation: Review the 11 new identities, then accept
decisions.answer: Review the 11 new identities, then accept
